annotations.text:
Kaam v2 — what changed and why

Today a worker can speak their availability but never see it; jobs appear without a yes/no; stats read ₹0 because the tiles call a council-only endpoint; finished jobs vanish. These five screens fix that without touching the voice loop.

Home v2 — the job needing a reply comes first (it is the only urgent thing), then a 7-day strip with three slots per day (morning / noon / evening) so the schedule is visible at a glance, then the mic as a shortcut into it, then real numbers and the last two jobs.
My week — the source of truth. Green = free, hatched = busy, dark = an accepted job, dashed = not set. Tap a block to remove it, mark busy or change the time; the sheet shows which sentence created it.
Job states — assigned → accept / can’t do it (with a reason the engine can learn from) → accepted with call, directions, running late → done with the 85/10/5 split.
Jobs & earnings — the cooperative story in numbers: your 85%, the 10% and the 5% fund, ratings and why they matter, passed-on jobs with no penalty.
After sign-up — new workers wait for council approval instead of being instantly matchable; they use the wait to set availability.

Backend needed

• GET /workers/me/summary — jobs, share, rating, active days (replaces the council-only dashboard call)
• DELETE /workers/{id}/availability/{index} and PATCH for start/end/available
• POST /bookings/{id}/accept and /decline {reason} — decline puts the booking back to pending and re-runs allocation excluding that worker
• GET /bookings?mine=1&status=completed with ledger lines
• users.status = pending | active — council approves from Sabha; pending workers are skipped by the engine
• Parser: misspellings (tommorrow, tommorow), no-day → low confidence, ‘at 10’ → 2-hour window
